findings.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one in group.js: totalPages computed as Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 renders an empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2), so 'next' stays enabled and findMembers() returns 0 members

remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing GroupUser destroy callbacks/counter cache, leaving groups.user_count stale and breaking the new pagination UI (totalPages/showingLast wrong, phantom or hidden pages)
The remove_member spec only asserts group.users.count == 0 and never verifies group.reload.user_count, the invariant the pagination UI depends on
add_members silently drops unknown usernames and does not strip whitespace (e.g., 'bob, alice' fails to match ' alice'), returning success_json with no error feedback to the user
The client addMembers handler only uses .then(...) with no rejection handling, so a 422 (e.g., can_not_modify_automatic) or validation error fails silently with no UI feedback or list reload

The add-members input is never cleared after clicking Add (acknowledged as '// TODO: should clear the input'), so a second click re-submits the same usernames and the UI shows stale entries contradicting server state

The create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible] and never assigns alias_level, even though the new template renders the alias-level combo box for all groups and the client's asJSON() includes it, so chosen alias level is silently dropped on creation

GroupsController#members response shape changed to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with zero test coverage for meta.total/limit/offset, the default limit of 50, or offset handling for non-automatic groups (a behavioral change from pagination only applying to automatic groups)

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put :remove_member while the route registers DELETE, so the actual DELETE verb and routing (including nested group_id param) are never exercised and a verb/routing mismatch would pass CI

Public group members page is now truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI: new limit applies to every group, but next/previous controls were only added to the admin template, not the public members.hbs/route, so users cannot see members beyond the first page (regression from showing all/200 members)

Breaking, untraceable change to admin API payload shape: update action rewritten from nested params[:group] to flat top-level params and asJSON dropped the group: wrapper, so existing consumers sending group[alias_level] etc. cause visible to be silently flipped to false when params[:visible] is absent; changes:{add:...} consumers now hit update which ignores changes entirely

Off-by-one in totalPages calculation in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 = 3 pages instead of 2), leaving 'next' enabled and showing a zero-member page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

Cosmetic churn unrelated to the requirement: whitespace-only reformatting of two templates, ilike → ILIKE no-op, and SCSS refactor hoisting .badges form styles into a shared .groups, .badges scope that couples future groups-form edits with badge-page styling

Spec exercises remove_member via xhr :put instead of the correct DELETE verb (route is delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'), so the test passes only because functional tests bypass routing and does not verify a real DELETE request reaches the action; converting to a request spec would route to add_members and silently lose the 'cannot modify automatic groups' coverage

addMembers never clears the usernames selector input (acknowledged TODO), so a second click re-submits the same usernames; combined with the server silently returning success_json when zero usernames match real users, the admin gets no feedback that usernames like 'l77t' were never added
Deleted spec coverage for 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' was not ported to the new endpoint, removing regression protection for silent-skip behavior in add_members

groups_controller.rb create action reshapes the API payload (flat params[:name]/params[:visible]) and silently drops usernames input, breaking existing API consumers with 422s or empty groups without a version bump

groups_controller.rb update action ignores payload[:usernames] and the PATCH incremental changes:{add,delete} path is deleted, so callers get success_json (200) while no membership change occurs — a silent no-op
config/routes.rb removes GET /admin/groups/:id/users with no replacement or deprecation, causing routing 404s for existing consumers
groups_controller.rb members action has no upper clamp on limit, allowing limit=100000000 to materialize and serialize the entire group membership in one request on a hot path
groups_controller.rb members action passes negative offset straight through to ActiveRecord, causing PostgreSQL 'OFFSET must not be negative' errors and 500s
admin-group.js.es6 totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, producing a phantom empty page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count/limit)

admin-group.js.es6 next/previous fire findMembers() with no request sequencing or cancellation, so a stale response can overwrite members with the wrong page's data while the pager shows a different page

groups_controller.rb add_members silently skips unknown usernames (including names with leading spaces due to missing .strip) and still renders success_json, giving admins no signal that members failed to be added
groups_controller.rb add_members issues one User.find_by_username query per username in a loop (N+1) instead of a single batched User.where lookup, with unbounded N
group_member.hbs {{#unless automatic}} guard resolves against the member context (which has no automatic property) instead of the group, so the remove affordance renders for automatic groups too
removeMember in the controller has no .catch/error handling, so clicking remove on an automatic group produces an unhandled 422 rejection with no user feedback

group.js findMembers returns undefined (instead of a promise resolving to an array) on empty name and on the success path, breaking callers written against the old contract that expect a resolved array

The PATCH incremental-membership API (update_patch) was deleted from config/routes.rb and admin/groups_controller.rb without acknowledgment, breaking external consumers performing incremental membership changes with 404 errors

The update action request payload shape changed from nested group[name]/group[usernames] to flat name/alias_level/visible, and old nested format requests return 200 success while the membership change is silently dropped

createWithUsernames was removed from group.js and the create action no longer accepts group[usernames], so creating a group with initial members silently creates an empty group and returns 200 with usernames discarded

Non-automatic groups were silently truncated from full member list to 50 members in groups_controller#members, with no pagination UI added to the public group members template, leaving groups with >50 members showing an incomplete roster

totalPages in admin-group.js.es6 has an off-by-one error: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces a phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2)

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test uses xhr :put instead of delete, hitting the add_members endpoint instead of remove_member, so the test passes for the wrong reason and would not catch removal of the can_not_modify_automatic guard
add_members silently skips unknown usernames and reports success, so a typo'd username yields no error or warning and the admin believes the member was added

remove_member uses raw group.users.delete(user_id) bypassing Group#remove semantics, and the delete persists immediately even if the subsequent group.save fails, so the client receives 422 while the removal was actually persisted
Removing the last member on the final page strands the admin on an empty page: findMembers clamps the offset, receives 0 members, and the view renders an empty page with no auto-correction of offset
Unvalidated negative offset parameter reaches SQL in members action, causing OFFSET -1 and unhandled 500 error on public endpoint for custom groups
limit parameter has no upper clamp on public members endpoint, allowing resource-exhaustion DoS via large limit values like 99999999
params.require(:usernames) is not type-checked before .split, causing NoMethodError 500 when sent as array or hash instead of a 400/422
Individual usernames in add_members are never stripped or blank-rejected, so 'alice, bob' silently fails to add 'bob' while returning success

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb: the rewritten update action's primary (non-automatic) branch has zero test coverage — alias_level, visible, and non-automatic rename branches are untested, so regressions in the main update path would pass the suite

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-33: the members endpoint's response contract was rewritten to { members:, meta: { total, limit, offset } } with no test verifying the shape, while the client (group.js findMembers) hard-depends on those exact keys — drift would silently break pagination

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (.remove_member): the automatic-group guard test uses xhr :put while the diff wires the action as a DELETE route, so the DELETE route → remove_member mapping introduced in config/routes.rb is never verified

spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (.add_members): silent-skip semantics for nonexistent usernames in bulk add are untested — the diff deleted the old tests covering this behavior and only the happy path and 422 guard are covered

Admin groups controller create/update flipped API payload from nested group: {...} to flat params in the same commit that removes the old reader, with no compatibility window (expand+contract violation)
During rolling deploy, new client to old pod: update_put does payload = params[:group] then payload[:alias_level] on nil, causing NoMethodError 500

During rolling deploy, old cached client to new pod: params[:visible] is nil so group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" silently flips visible to false on every group save (data loss of the visible flag)
During rolling deploy, old cached client to new pod: create runs with params[:name] nil so group.name = "" causing save failure or creation of a blank-named group if validations allow

Groups controller members action changed response shape from a bare serialized array to a {members:, meta:} envelope with no dual-format period, breaking old cached JS (result.map is not a function) and new JS against old pods (result.members undefined)
External API consumers of GET /groups/:name/members break with no deprecation path due to the response shape change
Admin groups controller remove_member mutates the join table directly via group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing the Group#remove model path and skipping GroupUser-level callbacks/side effects

Membership removal via group.users.delete is committed immediately outside the subsequent group.save with no transaction or rollback, so a failed save leaves the member removed while the client sees a failure response
config/routes.rb removed the get "users" admin groups route in the same PR that introduces its replacement, with no overlap window, causing 404s for any un-migrated caller during rollout

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing GroupUser destroy callbacks/counter cache, leaving groups.user_count stale and breaking the new pagination UI (totalPages/showingLast wrong, phantom or hidden pages)
The remove_member spec only asserts group.users.count == 0 and never verifies group.reload.user_count, the invariant the pagination UI depends on

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a completed `remove_member` spec that “only asserts `group.users.count == 0`”; the new `.remove_member` context is truncated before any assertions are visible. Also, the pagination UI in this diff relies on `model.user_count` as set by `Group#findMembers()` from `GroupsController#members` (`meta.total = group.users.count`), not on a persisted `group.user_count` counter cache. After `removeMember`, the client calls `findMembers()` again, so `user_count` is refreshed from `group.users.count` regardless. Thus the finding is not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames and does not strip whitespace (e.g., 'bob, alice' fails to match ' alice'), returning success_json with no error feedback to the user

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, `usernames` is taken as a raw string and processed via `usernames.split(",").each do |username| ... User.find_by_username(username) ... end` with no `strip`/normalization. This means inputs like "bob, alice" will yield a second token " alice" that likely won’t match any user, so that member won’t be added. Additionally, if a username doesn’t exist (or has leading/trailing spaces), it is simply skipped (`if user = ...`) and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, providing no error/feedback that some usernames were ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client addMembers handler only uses .then(...) with no rejection handling, so a 422 (e.g., can_not_modify_automatic) or validation error fails silently with no UI feedback or list reload

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6` just calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and does not attach any `.then(...)`/`.catch(...)` at all. The model method `Group#addMembers` does use `.then(function() { self.findMembers(); })`, so on success it will reload the member list. On failure (e.g., server returns 422), that `.then` will not run, but whether the failure is “silent” or provides UI feedback depends on how `Discourse.ajax` handles rejected requests globally (not shown in the diff). Therefore the claim that it “fails silently with no UI feedback” is not verifiable from this diff, and the finding also inaccurately describes the handler as using `.then(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The add-members input is never cleared after clicking Add (acknowledged as '// TODO: should clear the input'), so a second click re-submits the same usernames and the UI shows stale entries contradicting server state

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and only calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting/clearing `this.usernames` (e.g., `this.set("usernames", null)` or similar). Since the template binds the `user-selector` to `usernames=usernames`, the entered usernames will remain in the input after a successful add, making a second click resubmit the same value and leaving stale UI state. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible] and never assigns alias_level, even though the new template renders the alias-level combo box for all groups and the client's asJSON() includes it, so chosen alias level is silently dropped on creation

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create the server only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` from `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` and never reads `params[:alias_level]`. Meanwhile the client `Discourse.Group#asJSON()` now includes `alias_level`, and `Discourse.Group#create()` POSTs `data: this.asJSON()`, so a selected alias level from the template’s combo-box will be sent but ignored, resulting in the created group using the default alias_level instead of the chosen value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupsController#members response shape changed to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with zero test coverage for meta.total/limit/offset, the default limit of 50, or offset handling for non-automatic groups (a behavioral change from pagination only applying to automatic groups)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupsController#members` to return `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` and applies `limit`/`offset` pagination to all groups with a default `limit` of 50 (previously pagination was only applied to automatic groups, and the response was `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` without meta). However, the proposed finding frames this as a “problem” mainly because there is “zero test coverage” for the new meta fields/default limit/offset behavior. Lack of tests is not a concrete defect introduced by the diff, and the behavioral change itself may be intentional (the JS client was updated to consume the new shape). So while the observation is accurate, it doesn’t identify a clear, verifiable bug/correctness issue on its own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' spec issues xhr :put :remove_member while the route registers DELETE, so the actual DELETE verb and routing (including nested group_id param) are never exercised and a verb/routing mismatch would pass CI

Public group members page is now truncated to 50 members with no pagination UI: new limit applies to every group, but next/previous controls were only added to the admin template, not the public members.hbs/route, so users cannot see members beyond the first page (regression from showing all/200 members)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, for all groups (previously only automatic groups were limited, and non-automatic returned all members). On the client, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset` and sets `members` from the returned page. The public route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now just calls `model.findMembers()` once, and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}` but no pagination controls/actions were added there (the next/previous UI was added only in the admin template/controller). Result: the public members page will show only the first 50 members with no way in the public UI/route to request subsequent pages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking, untraceable change to admin API payload shape: update action rewritten from nested params[:group] to flat top-level params and asJSON dropped the group: wrapper, so existing consumers sending group[alias_level] etc. cause visible to be silently flipped to false when params[:visible] is absent; changes:{add:...} consumers now hit update which ignores changes entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the admin group API contract in a way that will break existing callers. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` no longer read nested `params[:group]` (old code used `payload = params[:group]` and `params[:group][:name]`, etc.) and instead expect flat top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`). On the client, `Discourse.Group#asJSON` similarly drops the `{ group: {...} }` wrapper and sends a flat hash. Any existing consumer still sending `group[visible]`, `group[alias_level]`, etc. will now result in those being ignored; specifically `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to `false` when `params[:visible]` is absent. Also, the previous PATCH-based incremental membership update (`update_patch` handling `params[:changes]`) is removed; `#update` no longer checks `request.patch?` and ignores `params[:changes]` entirely, so prior `changes:{add/delete}` clients would no longer work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages calculation in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 = 3 pages instead of 2), leaving 'next' enabled and showing a zero-member page; should be Math.ceil(user_count / limit)

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 when user_count > 0. If user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 and 50), this computes 3 pages instead of 2. The `next` action also allows offset to reach `user_count` (offset = Math.min(offset+limit, user_count)), and Group.findMembers then requests that offset, which will return an empty members list. Because showingLast is based on currentPage == totalPages, page 2/3 will keep “next” enabled, allowing navigation to this empty page. Using Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (and/or clamping offset to user_count - limit) would avoid the extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cosmetic churn unrelated to the requirement: whitespace-only reformatting of two templates, ilike → ILIKE no-op, and SCSS refactor hoisting .badges form styles into a shared .groups, .badges scope that couples future groups-form edits with badge-page styling

adjudication.rationale: The cited items are present (template indentation/whitespace adjustments, `ilike`→`ILIKE` which is functionally equivalent in Postgres, and SCSS moving `.form-horizontal` styling into a shared `.groups, .badges` block). However, these are primarily refactors/cosmetic churn and an arguably intentional stylesheet deduplication. The claim about “coupling future groups-form edits with badge-page styling” is speculative and not a clear defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec exercises remove_member via xhr :put instead of the correct DELETE verb (route is delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'), so the test passes only because functional tests bypass routing and does not verify a real DELETE request reaches the action; converting to a request spec would route to add_members and silently lose the 'cannot modify automatic groups' coverage

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the admin route for removing a member is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` while adding members is `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` (config/routes.rb). However, the controller spec begins a `.remove_member` context and calls the action with `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, ...` (spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb). In an RSpec controller spec this will invoke the `remove_member` action directly with a PUT request method, bypassing routing, so it does not actually verify that a real DELETE request to the routed endpoint reaches `remove_member` (and a real PUT to the endpoint would instead route to `add_members`). This is a real mismatch/coverage defect in the test introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers never clears the usernames selector input (acknowledged TODO), so a second click re-submits the same usernames; combined with the server silently returning success_json when zero usernames match real users, the admin gets no feedback that usernames like 'l77t' were never added

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6` that explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and never resets `this.get("usernames")` after submitting, so clicking the Add button again will resubmit the same usernames. On the server, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users that exist, but if none match it still proceeds to `group.save` and renders `success_json` (no error or feedback about unmatched usernames). This combination can lead to repeated “successful” submissions where nothing is actually added and the UI gives no indication why.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted spec coverage for 'succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' was not ported to the new endpoint, removing regression protection for silent-skip behavior in add_members

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous spec case `it "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` under the old incremental PATCH update behavior, and there is no equivalent test added for the new `add_members` endpoint. The new `add_members` implementation still silently skips unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), but the regression-protection test for that behavior was not ported, so coverage for this edge case is indeed lost in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb create action reshapes the API payload (flat params[:name]/params[:visible]) and silently drops usernames input, breaking existing API consumers with 422s or empty groups without a version bump

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#create` to read `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` directly and removes any handling of `params[:group][:usernames]` (and nested `params[:group]` entirely). Previously it accepted `group: { name, usernames, visible }` and could create a group with initial members. With the new code, an existing client still sending the old nested payload will result in `group.name` becoming `''` (since `params[:name]` is nil), likely causing `group.save` to fail and `render_json_error` (422). Even if a client sends usernames, they are now ignored in `create`, requiring a separate `add_members` call. This is a real, diff-verifiable backward-incompatible API change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb update action ignores payload[:usernames] and the PATCH incremental changes:{add,delete} path is deleted, so callers get success_json (200) while no membership change occurs — a silent no-op

adjudication.rationale: The diff deliberately removes membership updates from the admin groups `update` endpoint: `update_patch` (PATCH changes:{add,delete}) is deleted, `update` no longer reads `params[:group][:usernames]`, and new dedicated endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member` are added and wired in routes. Corresponding JS is updated to call `group.addMembers()`/`removeMember()` and to call `group.save()`/`create()` without usernames. There is no evidence in the diff of any remaining in-repo caller still sending `usernames` or PATCH `changes`, so describing this as a bug/no-op for callers is speculative/backwards-compatibility concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb removes GET /admin/groups/:id/users with no replacement or deprecation, causing routing 404s for existing consumers
groups_controller.rb members action has no upper clamp on limit, allowing limit=100000000 to materialize and serialize the entire group membership in one request on a hot path

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, the members action now does `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then `group.users...limit(limit)`, returning `serialize_data(members, ...)` in JSON. There is no max clamp/validation on `limit`, so a request can supply an arbitrarily large limit (e.g. 100000000) causing a very large query and serialization workload. The diff also removes the prior conditional pagination for only automatic groups and applies limit/offset to all groups, making this unbounded limit parameter broadly applicable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members action passes negative offset straight through to ActiveRecord, causing PostgreSQL 'OFFSET must not be negative' errors and 500s

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the code sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. If a client supplies a negative `offset` (e.g. `-1`), `to_i` preserves it and ActiveRecord will emit `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`OFFSET must not be negative`), resulting in an exception/500. The diff does not add any server-side guard against this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1, producing a phantom empty page whenever user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should be Math.ceil(user_count/limit)

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages returns Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1 (when user_count > 0). If user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 50 users, limit 50), this computes 2 pages instead of 1, creating a phantom extra page. This is verifiable with the paired pagination logic: the next action can set offset to exactly user_count, and findMembers will request that offset, yielding an empty members list for the extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 next/previous fire findMembers() with no request sequencing or cancellation, so a stale response can overwrite members with the wrong page's data while the pager shows a different page
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers() is asynchronous and not properly handled, leading to race conditions. The candidate elaborates on the same underlying issue in the pagination context: without sequencing/cancellation, an earlier async response can arrive late and overwrite the current members data (stale data), which is a concrete manifestation of the golden’s ‘async unhandled’ race condition concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb add_members silently skips unknown usernames (including names with leading spaces due to missing .strip) and still renders success_json, giving admins no signal that members failed to be added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and looks up users via `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. Any unknown username (or one with leading/trailing spaces) is silently skipped because the `if user = ...` guard simply does nothing when not found. After the loop it calls `group.save` and renders `success_json` on success, which will still be true even if zero users were added, giving no indication that some/all requested additions failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb add_members issues one User.find_by_username query per username in a loop (N+1) instead of a single batched User.where lookup, with unbounded N

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop calls `User.find_by_username(username)`. That results in one DB query per username (potentially many) rather than a single batched lookup (e.g., `User.where(username: [...])`). The diff shows no validation or cap on the number of usernames passed, so the number of queries is effectively unbounded based on request input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs {{#unless automatic}} guard resolves against the member context (which has no automatic property) instead of the group, so the remove affordance renders for automatic groups too
removeMember in the controller has no .catch/error handling, so clicking remove on an automatic group produces an unhandled 422 rejection with no user feedback

group.js findMembers returns undefined (instead of a promise resolving to an array) on empty name and on the success path, breaking callers written against the old contract that expect a resolved array
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers can return undefined due to missing/implicit returns on certain code paths (e.g., empty name/success path), rather than returning an expected value (array/promise). This aligns with the golden issue about code paths without explicit returns yielding undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The PATCH incremental-membership API (update_patch) was deleted from config/routes.rb and admin/groups_controller.rb without acknowledgment, breaking external consumers performing incremental membership changes with 404 errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the `update_patch` method and removes the code path that handled `params[:changes]` incremental membership updates. However, this does not remove the PATCH route: `resources :groups` still provides `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` routed to `Admin::GroupsController#update`. So callers won’t get 404s; instead, their PATCH requests would still hit `#update` but membership changes via `changes[add/delete]` would be ignored (behavior change, not a routing 404). The claim about 404 errors is not verifiable from the diff and is incorrect given standard Rails routing here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update action request payload shape changed from nested group[name]/group[usernames] to flat name/alias_level/visible, and old nested format requests return 200 success while the membership change is silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Admin::GroupsController#update the diff changes the accepted params from a nested `params[:group]` payload (previously `payload = params[:group]` and `group.usernames = payload[:usernames]`) to flat top-level params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) and completely removes any handling of `usernames`/membership in `update`. Therefore an old client sending `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `group: { usernames: ... }` will have that membership change ignored (since `params[:group]` is never read), yet `group.save` will still typically return true (even with no changes), resulting in a 200 success response while the membership update is silently dropped. Membership changes are now only possible via the new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: createWithUsernames was removed from group.js and the create action no longer accepts group[usernames], so creating a group with initial members silently creates an empty group and returns 200 with usernames discarded

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `createWithUsernames`/`saveWithUsernames` from `group.js` and changes the admin group create/update APIs to accept top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, etc.) while no longer reading `params[:group][:usernames]` (or any `usernames`) in `Admin::GroupsController#create`. As a result, any caller still sending usernames during create (as the previous code/tests did) will get a 200 response but the group will be created without members because the usernames are ignored; membership is now only handled via the new `add_members` endpoint. This is a verifiable behavioral regression/backwards-incompatible change with silent discarding of provided usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-automatic groups were silently truncated from full member list to 50 members in groups_controller#members, with no pagination UI added to the public group members template, leaving groups with >50 members showing an incomplete roster

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes behavior from returning all members for non-automatic groups to always applying `limit` (default 50) and `offset`, returning only a page plus meta (`total/limit/offset`). On the public side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` switches to iterating `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination controls/actions are added there (unlike the admin template `admin/templates/group.hbs`, which adds next/previous UI). As a result, groups with >50 members will only show the first 50 with no way to navigate to the rest in the public members view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages in admin-group.js.es6 has an off-by-one error: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 produces a phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2)

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' test uses xhr :put instead of delete, hitting the add_members endpoint instead of remove_member, so the test passes for the wrong reason and would not catch removal of the can_not_modify_automatic guard

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the new route maps DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to `groups#remove_member` and PUT to `groups#add_members`. However the spec line shown uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`. In a Rails controller spec, the second argument (`:remove_member`) invokes that controller action directly; it does not “hit the add_members endpoint” based on the HTTP verb, because routing isn’t being exercised. So while the HTTP verb in the test is inconsistent with the routes (a test quality issue), the claim that it would pass for the wrong reason by calling `add_members` is not verifiably true from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips unknown usernames and reports success, so a typo'd username yields no error or warning and the admin believes the member was added

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. Unknown/typo’d usernames are simply ignored (no error collection). The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so the client gets a success response even if none/some of the requested usernames were actually added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses raw group.users.delete(user_id) bypassing Group#remove semantics, and the delete persists immediately even if the subsequent group.save fails, so the client receives 422 while the removal was actually persisted

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and only afterwards checks `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`. On an ActiveRecord association, `delete` issues a DELETE on the join row immediately (it is not staged on the parent and does not depend on `group.save`). Therefore, if `group.save` returns false for any reason (validations/callbacks), the controller will respond with 422 even though the membership removal has already been persisted. This is a real correctness/consistency risk introduced by the diff. The claim about bypassing Group#remove semantics is plausible but not directly verifiable from the diff since Group#remove isn’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing the last member on the final page strands the admin on an empty page: findMembers clamps the offset, receives 0 members, and the view renders an empty page with no auto-correction of offset
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: clamping/capping the pagination offset to the total/user_count can result in an offset equal to the total, yielding an empty result set and rendering an empty last page (confusing UX). The candidate adds a specific trigger (removing the last member) but the core issue matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated negative offset parameter reaches SQL in members action, causing OFFSET -1 and unhandled 500 error on public endpoint for custom groups

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. If a client supplies `offset=-1`, `to_i` yields `-1` and Rails will generate SQL with `OFFSET -1` (Postgres rejects negative OFFSET), causing a 500 on this public `/groups/:group_id/members.json` endpoint. There is no server-side clamp to `>= 0` (only a client-side clamp exists in `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, which does not protect the endpoint).

adjudication_records.issue_text: limit parameter has no upper clamp on public members endpoint, allowing resource-exhaustion DoS via large limit values like 99999999

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies it directly: `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no upper bound/clamp on `limit`, so a client can pass an extremely large value (e.g. 99999999) causing the server to attempt a very large DB read and serialize a huge member list, which is a plausible resource-exhaustion/DoS vector on this public (non-admin) endpoint (guarded only by `ensure_can_see!`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: params.require(:usernames) is not type-checked before .split, causing NoMethodError 500 when sent as array or hash instead of a 400/422

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. `params.require` only enforces presence, not type. If a client submits `usernames` as an Array or Hash (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `usernames` will not be a String and will not respond to `split`, raising `NoMethodError` and resulting in a 500 instead of a handled 4xx. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Individual usernames in add_members are never stripped or blank-rejected, so 'alice, bob' silently fails to add 'bob' while returning success

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace or skipping blanks. Therefore an input like "alice, bob" produces tokens "alice" and " bob"; the second lookup will not match a real username "bob" (leading space), so that user won’t be added. The method also ignores non-existent users and still returns success_json if the group saves, so this failure is silent as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb: the rewritten update action's primary (non-automatic) branch has zero test coverage — alias_level, visible, and non-automatic rename branches are untested, so regressions in the main update path would pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `Admin::GroupsController#update` semantics (now reads params directly, handles `alias_level`, `visible`, and `name` with an `!group.automatic` guard), but the updated spec only adds a single `.update` example that exercises the *automatic* group branch (“ignore name change on automatic group”). The previous tests that covered updating a normal (non-automatic) group (including rename and membership updates) were removed, and no new test covers the primary non-automatic update path for `alias_level`, `visible`, or `name`. This is directly verifiable in the rewritten `context ".update"` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-33: the members endpoint's response contract was rewritten to { members:, meta: { total, limit, offset } } with no test verifying the shape, while the client (group.js findMembers) hard-depends on those exact keys — drift would silently break pagination

adjudication.rationale: The diff does rewrite `GroupsController#members` to return a JSON object with `members` and `meta` keys, and the client-side `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was updated to consume `result.meta.*` and `result.members`. However, the proposed finding claims this is a problem because there is “no test verifying the shape” and that drift “would silently break pagination.” That’s not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the server and client are currently in sync in this change, and the absence of a test in the shown diff is not proof that no such test exists elsewhere, nor is it a runtime bug by itself (it’s a hypothetical maintainability concern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (.remove_member): the automatic-group guard test uses xhr :put while the diff wires the action as a DELETE route, so the DELETE route → remove_member mapping introduced in config/routes.rb is never verified
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue flags the same mismatch as the golden comment: the remove_member controller spec uses `xhr :put`, but the route/action wiring expects a DELETE request (`delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (.add_members): silent-skip semantics for nonexistent usernames in bulk add are untested — the diff deleted the old tests covering this behavior and only the happy path and 422 guard are covered

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove prior specs that asserted “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” (previous incremental PATCH tests). The new `add_members` controller action still silently skips missing users (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), but the updated spec suite only covers the automatic-group guard (422) and a happy-path add. However, this is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable functional/security/correctness defect introduced by the code itself—runtime behavior still matches the prior semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups controller create/update flipped API payload from nested group: {...} to flat params in the same commit that removes the old reader, with no compatibility window (expand+contract violation)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete breaking API change: the JS model `Group.asJSON()` changed from `{ group: { ... } }` to a flat payload `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, and `Admin::GroupsController#create`/`#update` likewise changed from reading `params[:group][:...]` to reading top-level `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`. There is no fallback handling for the old nested `group` params, so any older client (or cached JS assets) still sending the previous shape would fail against the updated server (and vice versa). This is exactly an expand+contract/compatibility-window violation and is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: During rolling deploy, new client to old pod: update_put does payload = params[:group] then payload[:alias_level] on nil, causing NoMethodError 500

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the client/server parameter contract for updating groups. New client code calls `group.save()` which sends `data: this.asJSON()` (flat keys: `name`, `alias_level`, `visible`) instead of the old `data: { group: {...} }`. In the old server code shown removed in this diff, `update_put` did `payload = params[:group]` and then immediately accessed `payload[:alias_level]`, which would raise `NoMethodError` if `params[:group]` is missing. During a rolling deploy where a new client hits an old server pod, that crash is a real, specific incompatibility introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: During rolling deploy, old cached client to new pod: params[:visible] is nil so group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" silently flips visible to false on every group save (data loss of the visible flag)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff changes the parameter shape from `payload = params[:group]` to reading top-level params (`params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:name]`). It unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. If `params[:visible]` is absent (e.g., old client still sending `group: { visible: "true" }`, or any caller omitting `visible`), `params[:visible]` is `nil` and the expression evaluates to `false`, flipping `visible` off on save. This is a concrete behavior change introduced by the diff and matches the rolling-deploy incompatibility described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: During rolling deploy, old cached client to new pod: create runs with params[:name] nil so group.name = "" causing save failure or creation of a blank-named group if validations allow

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the admin group create API contract. Server-side `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]` and defaults to `''` when missing (`group.name = (params[:name] || '').strip`). Previously it expected `params[:group][:name]` (nested under `group`). An old cached client (pre-diff) would still POST `{ group: { name: ... } }`, so `params[:name]` would be nil on the new server, resulting in `group.name` becoming an empty string and `group.save` failing (or, if validations allowed, potentially creating a blank-named group). This is a real backwards-compatibility issue introduced by the diff during rolling deploys.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Groups controller members action changed response shape from a bare serialized array to a {members:, meta:} envelope with no dual-format period, breaking old cached JS (result.map is not a function) and new JS against old pods (result.members undefined)
External API consumers of GET /groups/:name/members break with no deprecation path due to the response shape change

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, the `members` action changes from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which would return a plain serialized collection/array response) to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. This is a concrete, incompatible response-shape change for GET `/groups/:name/members` (now `/members.json` in the JS call, but the controller action still serves the same route). The diff shows no compatibility wrapper, versioning, or alternate endpoint to preserve the prior output, so any external consumer expecting the old top-level array/format would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin groups controller remove_member mutates the join table directly via group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing the Group#remove model path and skipping GroupUser-level callbacks/side effects

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` using `group.users.delete(user_id)` instead of the previously used `group.remove(user)` path (seen earlier in the removed `update_patch` code). However, the claim that this "bypasses Group#remove" and "skips GroupUser-level callbacks/side effects" is not verifiable from the diff: we are not shown any `Group#remove` implementation or any join-model callbacks/side effects that would be missed. Without evidence in the changed codebase that such callbacks exist and are required, this is a speculative concern rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Membership removal via group.users.delete is committed immediately outside the subsequent group.save with no transaction or rollback, so a failed save leaves the member removed while the client sees a failure response

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the code performs `group.users.delete(user_id)` before checking `if group.save`. `group.users.delete` issues an immediate DELETE on the join table (persists the membership change independently of the parent model). The subsequent `group.save` is a separate operation and is not wrapped in a transaction; if `group.save` were to fail for any reason (validations/callbacks), the controller would return an error response even though the member has already been removed, with no rollback of the deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb removed the get "users" admin groups route in the same PR that introduces its replacement, with no overlap window, causing 404s for any un-migrated caller during rollout

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an `admin/groups` nested route (`get "users"`) and adds new `put "members"` / `delete "members"` routes, but the proposed finding’s claimed impact (“causing 404s for any un-migrated caller during rollout”) depends on the existence of external or not-yet-updated callers, which is not shown in the diff. Within the diff itself, there’s no reference to the removed `get "users"` route, and the newly added routes are not a direct GET replacement for it. So the breakage scenario is not directly verifiable from the provided changes.
